plan: Reduce QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and concentrating on income and broad index exposure, aiming for low drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to slightly reduce income concentration.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels (3% and 1%).
Trim 2x leveraged ETFs (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to reduce sector leverage.
Add RTX as a new position at 4% from the scanner.
This balances risk reduction with some growth exposure.
A small cash buffer is maintained for opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly return by reducing leverage and concentration while adding a promising new name. It aims for risk-first growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer and keeping overall leverage in check.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% while maintaining income exposure.
Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.
Increase 2x leveraged ETFs (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Add RTX as a new position at 6% from the scanner.
This plan concentrates exposure in high-conviction areas.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by increasing leveraged ETF exposure and concentrating in high-scoring scanner setups. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the daily rebalancing decay of leveraged ETFs, requiring strict stop discipline.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Sell all 2x AI/Software and Semiconductor ETFs (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Sell high-beta tech names (CRWD, SNOW) to reduce volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing capital preservation and reliable income. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leverage and high-beta single names, focusing on income-generating ETFs and a cash buffer.
